it was published from, and whether or not it may be pinned.
Renamed from inherited-releases.json on 2026-08-30. The old name stopped
covering the file's job the moment this repository published one of its own:
the release floor is derived from everything here, and a version published
HERE bounds the floor exactly as an inherited one does. Keeping the old name
and adding a non-inherited row would have made the filename a lie.
`pinnable = false` means the version exists permanently and must never be
depended on. That is not the same as absent, and the distinction is the whole
reason this file lists it: an index cannot un-publish, so the only place a
'do not pin this' fact can live is here and in the guard that reads it.

bearing rather than tidy: the release floor is derived as the maximum of

Published by run 33297423568 from the exact tip of protected main. Its tag was written in that same run by a job that called itself a verification and could not perform one: it compared hashes over whatever `pip download` returned (the wheel; never the sdist) and swallowed the install result with `|| true`. INDEPENDENT verify run 33310594187 later returned VERIFIED against the registry — both artifacts fetched by name and sha256-equal to the release run's build, provenance closed on peeled commit 2c61540f74018b7e19d7c5add893e0653cfcdb17, publisher read-back, read-only consumer install, and exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index. releases.unpinnable_reason: SUPERSEDED BY 0.1.0a5 FOR FUNCTIONAL REASONS, NOT IDENTITY ONES. a4's five identity proofs stand and are recorded above unchanged. It is refused here because it cannot be adopted: `approve_plan` refuses a correctly-supplied approval digest with "the plan changed after approval" whenever the caller uses the other encoding of the same digest (`propose_plan` stored bare hex, `spec_digest` produced the `sha256:`-prefixed form, and the comparison was between two strings), and the published wheel reports `__version__ == "0.1.0a2"` while declaring 0.1.0a4, so an authorization would record the wrong version of the deciding module. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: a4 remains immutable and identity-verified, and is UNADOPTABLE. Platform CP must pin 0.1.0a5, never 0.1.0a4.

disposition.functional_authorization_evidence: service.py:305 `snapshot_digest` returns bare hex; service.py:311 `spec_digest` returns `sha256:`-prefixed; service.py:889 `propose_plan` stores the bare form; service.py:974 `approve_plan` evaluates `evidence.content_digest != row.plan_digest`. A caller supplying the same digest in the other encoding is refused with "the plan changed after approval, so a new approval is required" — a security refusal standing in for a formatting bug.
disposition.version_self_reporting_evidence: __init__.py:172 declares `__version__ = "0.1.0a2"` while pyproject.toml declares 0.1.0a4. Two literals for one fact; nothing compared them because every check read the source tree rather than the built artifact.

releases.unpinnable_reason: SUPERSEDED BY 0.1.0a6 FOR ITS DECLARED DEPENDENCY FLOOR, NOT FOR ITS ARTIFACT IDENTITY OR ITS BEHAVIOUR. a5's seven verification properties stand and are recorded above unchanged: the bytes on the index are the bytes release run 33318227812 built, and the encoding defect a5 was cut for is genuinely fixed. It is refused here because it cannot be COMPOSED. `service.py:73` reads `from dotmac_kernel.transactions import conflict_savepoint`; `dotmac_kernel/transactions.py` first shipped in dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a98 and is absent from the published 0.1.0a97 wheel, while a5's metadata declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a77)` — under-constrained by 21 alphas. The Platform CP lane resolved a kernel inside the declared range, wrote a clean lock, matched both published sha256 digests byte-for-byte, and raised ModuleNotFoundError at container boot. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: a5 is immutable and verified, and is UNDER-CONSTRAINED AND UNSUITABLE FOR NEW ADOPTION. Platform CP must pin 0.1.0a6 with dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a98, never 0.1.0a5.

disposition.artifact_identity_evidence: All seven properties, unchanged: the tag peels to b182a99892067f26c0c1d03d958c5fcdc97c5869; wheel sha256 c02804b1b9f6dab7becc21696efccdf3820de06dba50903568e2db4c966e0aec; sdist sha256 5883f8ead3caab1a5d93977e6f086ad0f9f2b9df3e5828b5380ea0c41d841ef8; publisher read-back; a read-only consumer installed it with its real dependency graph and imported it; exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index; and all seven behavioural canaries passed against the wheel the registry served. disposition.functional_authorization_evidence: The defect a5 was cut for is fixed and stays fixed. `PlanDigestV1` makes a digest a value rather than a string, `approve_plan` accepts a4's bare-hex encoding of the plan's own digest, and an unreadable digest raises `DigestEncodingError` rather than claiming the plan changed. Canaries `a4_bare_hex_still_binds` and `encoding_fault_is_not_a_mutation` proved it against the published wheel, and 0.1.0a6 keeps both.
disposition.declared_dependency_floor_evidence: service.py:73 `from dotmac_kernel.transactions import conflict_savepoint`. `dotmac_kernel/transactions.py` is ABSENT from the published dotmac_kernel-0.1.0a97-py3-none-any.whl and PRESENT in dotmac_kernel-0.1.0a98-py3-none-any.whl, both read from registry.dotmac.io. a5's wheel declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a77)`, so any resolver may satisfy it with a kernel that cannot import the module. Discovered by the Platform CP lane at container boot, after resolution succeeded, the lock wrote cleanly, and both artifacts matched their published hashes exactly.
disposition.adoption_eligibility_evidence: `pinnable: false`. release_guard.refusals() refuses 0.1.0a5 by NAME, distinctly from the floor, so depending on it is a decision somebody has to overrule rather than an omission. 0.1.0a6 declares `>=0.1.0a98` and CI proves that floor in both directions: a lane that installs the declared minimum literally, and a mutation lane that installs the newest kernel the floor excludes and requires the canaries to fail.

releases.release_run_note: THE FIRST RELEASE WHOSE DECLARED DEPENDENCY FLOOR IS ITSELF PROVEN, and the first verified on nine behavioural canaries rather than seven. Published by run 33322980430 from the exact tip of protected main (518711c36e9e5774e11b02c6ab35ec0c9c7b75b9); that run neither verified itself nor tagged. INDEPENDENT verify run 33323067886 returned VERIFIED on all seven properties: both artifacts fetched from registry.dotmac.io by NAME and sha256-equal to the release build, provenance closed on the peeled commit, publisher read-back, a read-only consumer install WITH the real dependency graph, import, exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index, and all NINE behavioural canaries passing against the wheel the REGISTRY served. Only that run wrote the tag, on a VERIFIED verdict, through tag_once.py. WHAT IS NEW HERE AND WAS NOT TRUE OF a5: the wheel declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a98)`, and that floor is proven in BOTH directions by the required `behavioural canaries (installed wheel)` context on commit 518711c3. The floor lane installed the wheel with dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a98 EXACTLY — the declared minimum, not the resolver's choice — and all nine canaries passed. The mutation lane derived 0.1.0a97 from the index as the newest kernel the floor excludes, observed pip refuse the pairing with `ERROR: Cannot install dotmac-deployment-control==0.1.0a6 and dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a97 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies`, then FORCED a97 in with --no-deps --force-reinstall and observed all nine canaries fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotmac_kernel.transactions'`. Supersedes 0.1.0a5, which remains immutable, verified on seven properties, and UNDER-CONSTRAINED AND UNSUITABLE FOR NEW ADOPTION.

Recorded here because the obligation is created by this release and discharged by its consumer.

releases.release_run_note: THE FIRST RELEASE THAT PUBLISHES THIS MODULE'S OWN DATABASE STRUCTURE, and the first whose floor mutation DERIVES both the excluded kernel and the module that exclusion must fail on. Published by run 33507951778 from the exact tip of protected main (6b1ce371b07220914696243647aeb0d3947b87cc); that run neither verified itself nor tagged. INDEPENDENT verify run 33508897684 returned VERIFIED on all seven properties: both artifacts fetched from registry.dotmac.io by NAME and sha256-equal to the release build (wheel 63,575 bytes, sdist 59,818 bytes), provenance closed on the peeled commit, publisher read-back (HTTP 200), a read-only consumer install as ci-reader WITH the real dependency graph, import, exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index, and all NINE behavioural canaries passing against the wheel the REGISTRY served. Only that run wrote the tag, on a VERIFIED verdict, through tag_once.py — "dotmac-deployment-control-v0.1.0a7 does not exist yet; writing it on 6b1ce371b07220914696243647aeb0d3947b87cc". WHAT a7 CARRIES: the source-owned `ModuleDatabaseCatalogContributionV1` that publishes mod_deploy's exact extent — seven platform tables and 95 columns, with PostgreSQL type identity and modifiers, physical ordinals, nullability, server defaults and relation kinds — authored from the frozen migration lineage rather than introspected at runtime. WHAT IS NEW IN THE VERIFICATION AND WAS NOT TRUE OF a6: the declared floor rises to >=0.1.0a100 because `database_catalog.py` imports `dotmac_kernel.product_database_catalog`, and BOTH halves of the mutation are now DERIVED rather than written down. On CI run 33488407034, on the release commit 6b1ce371, the required `behavioural canaries (installed wheel)` context installed the wheel with dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a100 EXACTLY — the declared minimum, not the resolver's choice — and all nine canaries passed, `declared_kernel_floor` reporting "installed EXACTLY 0.1.0a100 (product_database_catalog.py present)". The mutation lane then derived 0.1.0a99 from the index as the newest kernel the floor excludes, and `scripts/kernel_floor.py symbol` derived `dotmac_kernel.product_database_catalog` as the one module whose recorded introduction equals the declared floor; pip refused the pairing with "ERROR: Cannot install dotmac-deployment-control==0.1.0a7 and dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a99 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies", and a99 FORCED in with --no-deps --force-reinstall made all nine canaries fail with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotmac_kernel.product_database_catalog'". a6's literal would have demanded a failure naming `dotmac_kernel.transactions`, which a99 contains perfectly well — the lane would have gone red against a module with nothing wrong with it, or, on a near miss, green while proving nothing about the new boundary. WHAT THIS VERIFICATION DOES NOT COVER, stated because the canary set is the floor under "does this artifact work" and never a coverage claim: the nine canaries are the SAME NINE a6 shipped — installed_not_source, version_agreement, propose_emits_canonical, exact_digest_approves, a4_bare_hex_still_binds, encoding_fault_is_not_a_mutation, mutation_after_authorization_is_refused, declared_kernel_floor, conflict_savepoint_executes — and a7 adds none. NO canary drives the database catalogue against the registry-served wheel. The seven-table, 95-column extent is proven by source tests on the release commit (tests/architecture/test_database_catalog.py, including a clean-room PostgreSQL comparison), not by the artifact canaries, and must not be cited as artifact-level or production-adoption evidence. Supersedes 0.1.0a6, which remains published, verified and PINNABLE: a7 adds a capability and raises a floor, and does not withdraw anything a6 proved.
releases.adoption_note: Adopting a7 obliges a consumer to move to dotmac-kernel a100, and for Platform CP that is NOT a version bump. Kernel a100 makes `ProductAssemblySpec.api_documentation` MANDATORY — `create_app` raises RuntimeError when it is None, deliberately refusing to choose a default, because FastAPI publishes /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json unless told otherwise — and the field does not exist at a98 at all, so a consumer still on a98 cannot pre-satisfy it by passing a value. Adopting a7 is therefore the ADR-0016 cutover rather than a dependency bump, as the Platform CP lane measured on 2026-09-01. Recorded here for the same reason a6's note is: the obligation is created by this release and discharged by its consumer, and it must never be taken silently by a resolver. APPENDED 2026-09-01 by supplemental verify run 33517740717: adopting a7's DATABASE CATALOGUE by digest carries a second obligation, because the digest moves with the resolved kernel rather than with this wheel — see `supplemental_verify_runs[0].adoption_constraint`. Pinning the structure is safe across kernels; pinning the digest is not.

APPENDED, and it does not amend a single word of the original verification. Verify run 33508897684 drove NINE canaries, none of them the catalogue, and `release_run_note` still says exactly that because it remains true of that run. This is a SECOND run asking a question the first one did not.

Dispatched from main at 61611da881a5cd9c9a2a76d884655e610b52879d (PR #20), against the SAME published bytes: wheel b9534111a197ce818c3d0bac166f3a5a2857dc3ceb937cc9e53452e3d7ffcfb0, sdist d5ca7ae82469f57ae0b9443f579be5316dc3c31004a791a38c0bf5200f9e9b51, fetched from registry.dotmac.io by name. Nothing was published, rebuilt or re-uploaded; the run uploads nothing by construction. VERIFIED on all seven properties with ELEVEN canaries, the two new ones being `database_catalogue_as_published` and `catalogue_digest_binds`.

WHAT IS NOW PROVEN ABOUT THE ARTIFACT, and was previously proven only about the source: the wheel the REGISTRY served publishes mod_deploy's exact seven platform tables and 95 columns — every table identity in canonical order, every column by name, physical ordinal, PostgreSQL type identity AND rendered spelling, nullability, generation and server default, and every table's plane (`platform`) and owner (`module:deployment_control`). The canary compares identities, never counts: `len(tables) == 7 and len(columns) == 95` passes against a catalogue holding seven wrong tables, and CI run 33516330390 observed exactly that — a planted rename of `rollout_attempts` to `rollout_events` left both counts intact and was refused on identity, and a planted narrowing of `deployment_plans.plan_digest` to the dc_0001 width `character varying(64)` left every NAME correct and was refused on type. In both plants the other nine canaries still passed, which is what attributes each refusal to the catalogue rather than to a package that stopped importing.

The environment was proven, not assumed: sys.path carried only `scripts/`, the stdlib and /tmp/consumer/lib/python3.12/site-packages, and every catalogue module resolved inside site-packages — printed in the run's own output. The tag step reached `##[notice]dotmac-deployment-control-v0.1.0a7 already exists on 6b1ce371b07220914696243647aeb0d3947b87cc`, which is tag_once.py's ALREADY: a re-verification is not an error and never moves a tag.
supplemental_verify_runs.adoption_constraint: THE CATALOGUE DIGEST IS A COORDINATE OF (ARTIFACT, KERNEL), NOT OF THIS WHEEL ALONE, and a consumer adopting the structure by digest must pin both. The canonical module-catalogue document includes `manifest_contract_version`, and Deployment Control DECLARES NONE: `ModuleManifest.__post_init__` infers it from the kernel's own `KERNEL_MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION` at manifest construction. So a kernel that raises its manifest generation changes this digest while this wheel's bytes are untouched, and two correct parties holding the same artifact can compute different digests. sha256:92be901f... is the value observed with dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a100 installed, which is also the floor a7 declares. The canary deliberately does NOT pin the generation to a literal — that would turn a kernel bump into a red verification of an unchanged artifact — and requires only that it be a positive integer generation; `test_the_comparator_does_not_pin_the_kernels_manifest_generation` holds that limit open in both directions. The seven-table, 95-column STRUCTURE is what the canary pins, and it is stable across kernels; the digest over it is not.
